title: The Night the Ships Crossed Land

lines.text: On the morning of April 22, 1453, the defenders of Constantinople saw something impossible.
lines.spoken: On the morning of April twenty-second, fourteen fifty-three, the defenders of Constantinople saw something impossible.
lines.hero: the date, then the painting of the ships

lines.text: Ottoman warships, floating inside their own harbor.
lines.spoken: Ottoman warships, floating inside their own harbor.

lines.text: Three weeks earlier, they had sealed that harbor with a giant iron chain.
lines.spoken: Three weeks earlier, they had sealed that harbor with a giant iron chain.

lines.text: Stretched across the Golden Horn on wooden floats, it kept the Sultan's fleet out.
lines.spoken: Stretched across the Golden Horn on wooden floats, it kept the Sultan's fleet out.

lines.text: Mehmed the Second was 21 years old. He did not try to break it.
lines.spoken: Mehmed the Second was twenty-one years old. He did not try to break it.

lines.text: He built a road of greased logs over the hill behind Galata.
lines.spoken: He built a road of greased logs over the hill behind Galata.

lines.text: Then oxen and men dragged around 70 ships across dry land,
lines.spoken: Then oxen and men dragged around seventy ships across dry land,

lines.text: and slid them back into the water, behind the chain.
lines.spoken: and slid them back into the water, behind the chain.

lines.text: Now the harbor walls had to be guarded too, and the defenders were stretched even thinner.
lines.spoken: Now the harbor walls had to be guarded too, and the defenders were stretched even thinner.

lines.text: Five weeks later, on May 29, Constantinople fell.
lines.spoken: Five weeks later, on May twenty-ninth, Constantinople fell.

lines.text: A chain said to be from that harbor is still on display in Istanbul today.
lines.spoken: A chain said to be from that harbor is still on display in Istanbul today.
lines.hero: the chain photo, then the whole wall

fact_notes: Chain across the Golden Horn ordered 2 April 1453 (EBSCO Research Starters, Siege of Constantinople 1453).

22 April 1453: about 70 ships hauled overland on greased logs over the hill behind Galata/Pera into the Golden Horn (Britannica; Stanton, Medieval Maritime Warfare: 70-80; World History Encyclopedia: 70).
Mehmed II born 30 March 1432, so 21 in April 1453.
Defenders had to shift men to the Golden Horn walls, weakening the land defence (Stanton).
A chain attributed to the 1453 boom is displayed at the Istanbul Naval Museum; attribution is traditional, hence 'said to be'.
